advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Remove the tautological first assertion in test_module_size_lock_fails_closed_on_fetch_failure; keep only the meaningful `::warning::...` absence check.
evidence: assert "could not fetch main to verify the module-size limit lock" not in text or (
"::warning::could not fetch main to verify the module-size limit lock" not in text
# The offending warn-and-continue string must be gone entirely.
assert "::warning::could not fetch main to verify the module-size limit lock" not in text
advisory.finding: The first assertion in test_module_size_lock_fails_closed_on_fetch_failure is a logical tautology: `A not in text or B not in text` where B's string is a strict superset of A's, so if the warn string is absent both sides are true and the assertion can never fail meaningfully; only the second assertion actually verifies the contract.
advisory.suggested_fix: Delete the first `assert ... or ...` statement and retain only the assertion that the `::warning::could not fetch main to verify the module-size limit lock` string is absent.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Decide and document/handle the case where the branch deletes complexity-baseline.json entirely (treat as empty branch ceilings vs. hard error) so behavior matches the documented ratchet posture.
evidence: branch = load_baseline(BASELINE_PATH)
load_baseline raises SchemaError("baseline file not found: {path}") on FileNotFoundError (check_complexity_baseline.py:338-339)
README: '| Remove an entry | ✅ Allowed — the ratchet working |'
advisory.finding: When the branch deletes the entire complexity-baseline.json file, _run_lock calls load_baseline(BASELINE_PATH) which raises SchemaError ('baseline file not found') and returns 1, failing the lock. The README states removing entries is allowed (the ratchet); a full-file deletion is a different case that fails closed without an explanatory message distinguishing it, potentially surprising a contributor who legitimately drained all debt.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Use a consistent '::error::' annotation prefix for all fail-closed messages in _run_lock so both surface as CI annotations.
evidence: print(f"error: could not load base baseline from {base_path}: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
print(f"::error::{exc}", file=sys.stderr)  # fetch-failure branch
advisory.finding: In _run_lock the --base load-failure path prints a plain 'error:' prefix while the fetch-failure path prints a GitHub-annotation '::error::' prefix; the inconsistency means one failure surfaces as a CI annotation and the other does not, despite both being fail-closed conditions.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reject or warn when --base is supplied without --lock (e.g. validate in main) so the flag is not silently ignored.
evidence: parser.add_argument("--base", metavar="PATH", type=Path, ...)
group = parser.add_mutually_exclusive_group(required=True) covers --check/--update-stale/--lock only
main(): `if args.lock: return _run_lock(args.base)` — args.base is only consulted under --lock
advisory.finding: --base is declared as a top-level argument outside the mutually-exclusive group, so passing --base with --check or --update-stale is silently accepted and ignored rather than rejected, which could mislead a caller into thinking a base comparison occurred.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Assert the module-size gate fetch-failure branch positively fails closed (an `::error::...failing closed` line followed by `exit 1`), not merely that the old warn string is absent.
evidence: assert "::warning::could not fetch main to verify the module-size limit lock" not in text
Diff adds the positive contract: `echo "::error::could not fetch main to verify the module-size limit lock; failing closed."` then `exit 1` (_build-and-test.yml:390-391)
Absence rationale: no assertion in the test checks for `exit 1` or `failing closed` presence, so the fail-closed behavior is not verified — only the removal of one string is.
advisory.finding: test_module_size_lock_fails_closed_on_fetch_failure asserts only that the old warn-and-continue string is ABSENT from the workflow; it never asserts the positive fail-closed contract (an `::error::...failing closed` line followed by `exit 1`) that the diff introduces. A regression that removes the warn line but omits the `exit 1` — silently continuing on fetch failure — would still pass this test.
scenarios: A future edit deletes the warn line but forgets to add exit 1, reintroducing silent-continue on fetch failure — test stays green.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add assertions that the workflow contains `::error::could not fetch main to verify the module-size limit lock; failing closed.` and that its fetch-else branch contains `exit 1`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add tests (monkeypatching subprocess.run) covering _fetch_base_ceilings_from_main: fetch-failure -> LockFetchError/nonzero exit, unreadable base -> nonzero exit, and main-missing-baseline -> bootstrap exit 0.
evidence: Fail-closed branches: `if fetch.returncode != 0: raise LockFetchError(...)` (line 521), `if show.returncode != 0: raise LockFetchError(...)` (line 539), `except SchemaError ... raise LockFetchError(...)` (line 546)
Bootstrap allow: `if exists.returncode != 0: return None  # main has no baseline yet — bootstrap, allow` (line 532) driving _run_lock to print bootstrap message and `return 0` (lines 566-568)

Absence rationale: the only no-`--base` test (test_cli_lock_fails_closed_without_base_when_repo_unknown) returns before any git call; no test monkeypatches subprocess.run to simulate a failed fetch or a bootstrap (missing base) outcome.
advisory.finding: The fail-closed branches of _fetch_base_ceilings_from_main (git fetch returncode nonzero, git show failure, and parse_baseline SchemaError raising LockFetchError) and the bootstrap allow path (main lacks the baseline file -> return None -> exit 0) are untested. Only the GITHUB_REPOSITORY-unset branch is exercised. These are the central fail-closed and bootstrap contracts of the ticket.
scenarios: A refactor that turns a fetch failure into a silent success (e.g. mishandling returncode) or that makes the bootstrap path fail closed instead of allow would not be caught.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the skip-when-script-absent path in the Complexity-baseline lock step cannot be abused to bypass the lock by deleting/renaming the enforcing script in the same change (consider verifying the script's presence against main rather than exit 0).
evidence: `if [ ! -f scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py ]; then` ... `exit 0` (.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml:413-418)
The step comment frames this as a 'Definition-vs-tree skew guard (ticket ee2a): skip with a log line when the script is absent' (_build-and-test.yml:408-409)

Reachability: the branch under review could both edit .github/complexity-baseline.json (raise/add) AND remove scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py; the missing-file branch returns exit 0 before `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --lock` (line 419) ever runs, so the lock is bypassed. Bounded because the deletion is itself a reviewable diff, hence a defense-in-depth gap rather than an unconditional bypass.
advisory.finding: The Complexity-baseline lock workflow step fails OPEN (exit 0) when scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py is absent from the checked-out tree. A change that deletes or renames the enforcing script would silently pass the lock, letting a raised ceiling or new baseline entry that the same change introduces land without the administrator-override the lock is meant to require.
